Cite Gasperini et al. 2019, Cell 176(1-2):377-390. Kept git-ignored under data/knowledge/measured_unknown

join_amended: a pair id is compared after upper-casing its guide-group part and removing any Ensembl version from its gene part, on both sides: the readout table writes candidate-enhancer guide groups in upper case ('CHR1.10703_TOP_TWO:ENSG...') and the pair table in lower case ('chr1.10703_top_two:ENSG...'); TSS guide groups are written alike in both
what_was_read: before this amendment was written, of the fetched table: its header line (20 columns), and its pairs4merge column alone (identifiers: their pattern with digits masked, whether any carries an Ensembl version, and how many of the registered ids it holds before and after the case change). No value column (beta, intercept, fold change, any p-value, outlier_gene) was read
departure: the registration's STOP_RULE allows an amendment that changes column names only. The fold-change column is such a change. The join is not: without it no candidate-enhancer test joins at all (0 of the 872 registered ids are in the table as written, 345 after the case change), and it was decided from identifiers alone, before any value was read. It is stated here so the reader can weigh it; nothing else registered changes
unchanged: everything else registered: the population, the shortlist, the matching, the thresholds (p below 0.1, fold below 1), the treatment of unmeasured tests, the positive control, MIN_MATCHED, the bootstrap, the decision, the falsifier and every outcome sentence

inputs.role: the screen's readout: header and ids only
this run's registration, read before any reading

result_manifest.assembly: GRCh38 (the screen's hg19 elements lifted); distances in hg19 from the screen's table

bootstrap.unit: chromosome (the matched tests of one chromosome are drawn together)

parameters.join: a pair id is compared after upper-casing its guide-group part and removing any Ensembl version from its gene part, on both sides: the readout table writes candidate-enhancer guide groups in upper case ('CHR1.10703_TOP_TWO:ENSG...') and the pair table in lower case ('chr1.10703_top_two:ENSG...'); TSS guide groups are written alike in both

exclusions: the at-scale screen's tests in its pair table (GSE120861_gene_gRNAgroup_pair_table.at_scale), one per candidate-enhancer guide group 'top_two' and gene, lifted from hg19 to GRCh38 by measured_unknown.Chain at liftOver's default (95% of bases); excluded and counted: non-targeting groups, TSS and other control groups, the 'second_two' repeat groups, elements the design labels not_model_selected_* (entered because a pilot screen found a hit there), tests that do not lift, and repeated tests. Then INDEPENDENCE. Then the gene must be protein-coding in GENCODE v50 by its Ensembl id, and the element must overlap at least one compiled element (half-open, one base)

a test is excluded, and counted, when any row of either EPCrisprBenchmark file (training_K562 and heldout_5_cell_types, every dataset and cell type, read by coordinates, gene and dataset only) names the same gene (Ensembl id without version, or symbol) at an element overlapping the test's lifted element by at least one base. The remaining tests are independent of the benchmark pair by pair; the subset whose element overlaps no benchmark element at all is independent element by element and is read beside the primary
experimental rule lines of the compiled programs (signaltrace.PREDICTED_ONLY)

partitions.training: none of this test: the benchmark's rows are read only to exclude the tests they hold
partitions.heldout: the screen's tests independent of the benchmark; their readout is read once, if held

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 8a66a6e

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
